nodes.label: Lean CLAUDE.md index with @imports
nodes.rationale: Index stays thin and auto-loads modular rule files so every session has them without being told to read each.

nodes.label: Agent hard rules (no .env, no weakened DB guarantee, no edited migration)
nodes.rationale: Other agents do not auto-load CLAUDE.md imports, so the non-negotiables are restated in one place.
nodes.norm_label: agent hard rules (no .env, no weakened db guarantee, no edited migration)

nodes.label: Self-improving memory loop
nodes.rationale: Lessons accrue in lessons.md and load into every future session so the project gets harder to break while CLAUDE.md never bloats.

nodes.label: Where each kind of knowledge lives
nodes.rationale: A newcomer with no chat history must find any fact; nothing important may exist only in a conversation.

nodes.label: graphify-out code map
nodes.rationale: Committed GRAPH_REPORT.md, graph.json, graph.html give every agent the same map; a stale map is worse than none because it is trusted.

nodes.label: Three-layer API: routes -> services -> repositories -> Database
nodes.rationale: Each layer has one job and never reaches past the one below; one service method is one transaction; every repository method takes the actor scope.
nodes.norm_label: three-layer api: routes -> services -> repositories -> database

nodes.label: Object rules (classes with constructor injection, no module-level mutable state)
nodes.rationale: Project owner's instruction: stateful things are classes, stateless helpers are plain functions, no inheritance deeper than one level.
nodes.norm_label: object rules (classes with constructor injection, no module-level mutable state)

nodes.label: Database is the last line of defence
nodes.rationale: Guarantees hold even if application code is wrong; each has an attack test in packages/db/test/guarantees and must never be weakened.
nodes.norm_label: database is the last line of defence

nodes.label: Never insert into assets via Drizzle insert()
nodes.rationale: Drizzle names every column and sends default for omitted ones; Postgres checks privilege on every named column so status fails with 42501 by design. Use explicit SQL listing granted columns, then insert the registered movement in the same transaction.
nodes.norm_label: never insert into assets via drizzle insert()

nodes.label: Falsify, don't justify, before saying done

nodes.label: Approach A: modular monolith (TypeScript, Fastify, Drizzle, PostgreSQL, Compose)
nodes.rationale: Drizzle keeps every query visible as SQL so no-N+1 is checkable and does not obstruct exclusion constraints, partial unique indexes and RLS; small memory footprint for a shared VPS.
nodes.norm_label: approach a: modular monolith (typescript, fastify, drizzle, postgresql, compose)

nodes.label: Rejected approach B: NestJS with Prisma
nodes.rationale: Prisma hides SQL so N+1 is hard to see, and the Postgres features need raw SQL escapes anyway.
nodes.norm_label: rejected approach b: nestjs with prisma

nodes.label: Rejected approach C: Supabase hosted backend
nodes.rationale: Client data and identities would sit with a third party against the confidentiality promise, and the owner specified a Hostinger VPS.
nodes.norm_label: rejected approach c: supabase hosted backend

nodes.label: Invitation-only accounts and single-tenant deployment
nodes.rationale: Public sign-up is attack surface with no upside; one stack per client is simpler to prove than a tenant column on every table.

nodes.label: Partners book a model for a date range; staff assign the unit
nodes.rationale: Partners care about the model, not which unit; staff choice lets them rotate stock, avoid units due for repair and substitute on late returns.
